examples.explain: Counts match, but ']' arrives while '(' is still open.

hints: Counting each bracket type isn't enough - "([)]" has equal counts. What extra information matters?
When you see a closer, which opener must it match?
Push openers on a stack; on a closer, pop and check the type. At the end the stack must be empty.

insight.oneLiner: Push openers; every closer must match the top of the stack; valid iff the stack ends empty.

recall.a: The stack is empty, or the top opener is a different type.
recall.q: Two ways a closer can fail?

recall.a: The stack must be empty - leftover openers mean invalid.

insight.why: Valid bracket strings are nested structures, and the innermost unclosed bracket is exactly the stack's top.

oneLiner: Push openers; every closer must match the top of the stack; valid iff the stack ends empty.

pitfalls.explain: Return `not stack` at the end - '((' never fails a match but is still invalid.
pitfalls.title: Forgot unclosed openers

pitfalls.explain: Equal counts aren't enough: in '([)]' the brackets close in the wrong order.
pitfalls.title: Counted instead of matching

pitfalls.explain: A closer can arrive when nothing is open (e.g. ')('). Check the stack before popping.
pitfalls.title: Popped an empty stack

solutions.idea: Repeatedly remove '()', '[]' and '{}' until nothing changes. Valid strings vanish completely.
solutions.name: Delete adjacent pairs

footnotes.text: Last opened, first closed. Brackets nest, and nesting is exactly what a stack models: the innermost open bracket is always on top.

solutions.idea: Push openers; a closer must match and pop the top.
solutions.name: Stack

class Solution:
    def isValid(self, s: str) -> bool:
statement:
`s` contains only the characters `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{` and `}`. Return `true` if the brackets are **valid**:

1. Every opening bracket is closed by a bracket of the same type.
2. Brackets close in the correct order - the most recently opened one closes first.
3. Every closing bracket has a matching opener before it.
title: Valid Parentheses
